title: A predictive winner among models that share a false bridge
question: When candidate models share a bridge assumption across a disconnected network, does a predictive criterion computed on observed trials rank them by their cross-gap error?
design: Two disconnected subnetworks linked by exchangeable baselines with a design nuisance of varying size; three candidate models sharing the bridge ranked by leave-one-trial-out predictive density. 6 cells, 1000 replicates each.
answer: No. Candidate models that share the bridge had identical cross-gap bias (0 to 0.5 across scenarios), and the leave-one-trial-out winner was set by within-subnetwork structure: meta-regression won when a trial covariate changed the contrast, the common-effect model when not, with the same distribution at every bridge error. A predictive criterion on observed trials cannot rank models by an error they share.
findings: Refuting sentence fails: winner distribution independent of the bridge error (chi-square p 0.68 and 0.44).
Cross-gap bias -0.007 to 0.499, identical across candidates.
not_answered: Frequentist predictive densities rather than LOO-PSIS on ML-NMR; no grouped leave-subnetwork-out or synthetic deletion; population comparison not simulated. Peer review has not been done.
methods_compared: leave-one-trial-out log predictive density over three candidate models sharing an exchangeable-baseline bridge
